data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Slips as SPEEA Vote Ends Today
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) may be about to settle a labor issue before it can really become a problem today, as the Society of Professional Engineering Employees in Aerospace (SPEEA) is set to vote on the latest contract offer. There were signs that this could go in either direction, so the vote is being watched carefully. Investors, meanwhile, were a bit pessimistic, and sent Boeing shares down fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 6.53% loss in its share price over the past year.

Settling SPEEA

The good part about the SPEEA contracts is that the current one does not expire until early October. This means that, even if the contract as proposed today does not go through, there will still be an opportunity to renegotiate and potentially put a new one on the table for a vote before the contract even expires. This may not even be an issue, as reports note that Boeing has already offered terms to SPEEA that were better than many expected. Some elements, however, have previously suggested that Boeing's offer is insufficient as currently written, so the vote may go either way today.

More Tankers

Meanwhile, yesterday, we found out about a potential sale of KC-46A tankers to Qatar. It turns out that Qatar was not the only Middle East power with an eye on Boeing's tanker. The Israeli Air Force landed its second KC-46 tanker, known as the Gideon model after the Old Testament Bible hero. The KC-46 will be used to give Israeli fighter jets more operational range—a report from Israel Hayom calls the new range "unprecedented"—as well as more time aloft overall. More planes will be arriving, as the plane is the second of six that Israel recently purchased through its defense procurement delegation.

data.title: Amazon Stock (AMZN) Slips amid Plans to Invest $2 Billion in Latin America
data.description:
Prime Video, the streaming business of tech giant Amazon (AMZN), plans to invest more than $2 billion in Latin America from 2027 through 2030. The money will support original shows and movies as well as sports rights. Amazon also plans to more than double its number of locally produced originals compared with 2026, with more than 25 new titles scheduled for 2027 alone. The move comes as Prime Video's sports audience in Latin America has already topped 20 million households this year, which is more than it reached during all of 2025. Shares are down at the time of writing.

Nevertheless, the company's audience growth helps explain why Amazon is investing more in the region. Interestingly, the investment will focus on Mexico and Brazil. Argentina and Colombia are included as well, with Chile also part of the plan.

Prime Video is also focusing more on live sports because it gives viewers another reason to use the service regularly. For example, after Amazon signed an 11-year global NBA agreement, Prime Video expanded its coverage in Brazil and Mexico to more than 200 games per season. The NBA also became available through Prime Video in several additional Latin American markets.

Brazilian soccer is seeing similar growth. In fact, viewing hours for Copa do Brasil have more than doubled since it arrived on Prime Video. Amazon has also added Série A, which gives the service a larger role in Brazilian soccer.

Amazon Wants Prime Video to Become a Bigger Entertainment Hub

In addition, Prime Video plans to expand its third-party streaming subscriptions and movie rentals into more Latin American markets later this year. Customers will be able to subscribe to other streaming services directly through the Prime Video app. They will also be able to rent or buy movies without needing a Prime membership.

Amazon is investing behind the scenes as well. Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios are expanding training programs for local production workers and other creative talent. The goal is to build a larger production base in the region so Amazon can keep creating local content over the long term.

data.title: SNDK and BE: Citadel Has Already Cut 80% of Its Situational Awareness Risk
data.description:
Hedge fund Citadel has already removed more than 80% of the risk it took on after buying assets from Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness. In a letter obtained by CNBC, Citadel founder Ken Griffin said that the firm has completed more than 100 block trades worth over $4 billion. Those trades came after Situational Awareness was forced to sell its public stock positions in late July, which left Citadel with a large portfolio of AI-related investments to manage. This included large bets on flash-memory maker SanDisk (SNDK) and fuel-cell company Bloom Energy (BE).

It also included bets against software companies such as Adobe (ADBE) because Aschenbrenner believed that AI could hurt their businesses. However, the problem was that both sides of the strategy moved against the fund.

Indeed, SanDisk and Bloom Energy each fell more than 50% during the AI selloff. At the same time, software stocks such as Adobe recovered. Situational Awareness therefore lost money on both its long positions and its short bets. Those losses eventually triggered margin calls, which forced the fund to sell its public stock portfolio.

It was at this point that Citadel began discussions with Situational Awareness on July 29. One day later, it was reported that the fund had been forced to sell its public holdings. Citadel ultimately stepped in as a major buyer of those assets.

The Timing Worked in Citadel's Favor

Interestingly, the timing also ended up working in Citadel's favor. In fact, many AI-related stocks recovered after Situational Awareness was forced to sell. As a result, the late-July liquidation ended up occurring close to the bottom of the AI selloff. This helped Citadel's flagship Wellington fund gain 5.94% in July, which was its best monthly performance since 2022. Reuters also reported that Wellington's year-to-date return reached roughly 12%.

data.title: Disney Stock (NYSE:DIS) Notches Up Despite Lost Hopes for a Speedier Trial
data.description:
Entertainment giant Disney (DIS) is taking the fight directly to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), as it tries to block plans for early license review on its corporate-owned stations. But United States District Judge Loren AliKhan shut down hopes for a faster trial, refusing to provide a temporary restraining order. The news did not mean much concern to shareholders, though, as Disney shares notched up fractionally in Friday morning's trading. Disney has seen a 9.71% loss in its share price over the past year.

Not That Speedy a Trial

A Reuters report noted that Disney called on judges to issue a temporary restraining order on the FCC, keeping it from calling for early license review. But the FCC noted to Judge AliKhan that such a move was unnecessary, agreeing to provide 48 hours of notice before issuing orders to refer the Disney licenses for a hearing. The judge did note, however, that if the FCC did issue that hearing order, both sides would need to return to court the next day so that the court could hear arguments over a proper temporary restraining order. Disney did not comment on the matter, and the FCC seemed satisfied.

Not Lands, but Biomes

Disney has an unusual new plan prepared for its upcoming park in Abu Dhabi, as it plans to separate out the sections into "biomes" rather than its standard "lands." The park looks to incorporate the natural landscapes of Abu Dhabi, which includes the obvious sand as well as coral reefs, among other things. Early concept art includes a castle that looks more like a crystal spire than a traditional European castle. The design is unconventional, but that early concept art also provides a glimpse at a Disney park that is very much unlike the others in its arsenal. That could represent a major new draw at a time when Disney parks are starting to prove inaccessible for many regular park-goers.

data.title: To Help Lower Prices, Trump Removes Tariffs on Ground Beef Imports
data.description:
To help lower prices for consumers, U.S. President Donald Trump is allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of ground beef to be imported into America over the next three months free of tariffs. Trump said, "We have a commitment that this beef will be sold at 25% below current market prices." However, Trump did not say which companies had made commitments to sell ground beef at a discount.

The National Cattlemen's Beef Association, a lobby group, criticized the move, saying it would not address Trump's stated intention of helping consumers or lead to another claim Trump made that removing tariffs would increase the size of the U.S. beef herd. Beef imports into the U.S. currently face an average tariff of 26.4%.

Cattle Herds and Beef Prices

Beef prices in the U.S have soared this year as America's cattle herd steadily declines due to years of drought and high feed costs. Recent data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics shows that lean ground beef averaged $8.41 per pound in July of this year, while beef steaks averaged $12.00 to $13.50 per pound depending on the cut of meat.

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the U.S. cattle herd now stands at its smallest size since the 1950s, when America's population was half its size today. The number of cattle slaughtered in the U.S. has declined to 2.2 million this year, down from 2.5 million a year ago. Beef production in America has fallen by 300,000 pounds to 1.9 million over the same time frame, pushing prices higher.

data.title: Uber Stock Rises Despite $966 Million Fine from Dutch Regulators
data.description:
Shares of Uber (UBER) are rising today even though the ride-hailing company faces an €825 million ($966 million) fine. This comes after the Dutch Data Protection Authority ruled that Uber improperly used automated systems to suspend some drivers by not providing enough human review and by failing to properly explain some decisions. According to Reuters, the penalty would be the second-largest ever issued under Europe's GDPR privacy rules. Uber strongly disagrees with the decision and plans to appeal.

Summer Sale - Claim 70% Off TipRanks

High conviction META bears now have this Tradr ETF

Interestingly, the case covers incidents between 2020 and 2022. During that period, Uber's systems sometimes suspended drivers after detecting possible fraud. For example, the system could flag a driver if it believed the driver took unnecessary detours to increase a fare. It could also flag someone who accepted trips without intending to complete them.

The problem is that European privacy law places limits on major decisions made entirely by computer systems. If an automated decision can seriously affect someone's life or job, regulators generally require meaningful human review. People must also have a way to challenge the decision. Dutch regulators concluded that Uber did not meet those requirements in some cases.

Unsurprisingly, Uber disputes that finding. The company says that temporary suspensions were generally short. It also says that permanent fraud-related account removals required human review. Uber added that its current policies allow drivers to dispute suspensions. In addition, since Uber plans to appeal, the $966 million headline number may not end up being the company's final cost.

Why the Size of the Fine Stands Out

Nevertheless, Uber argues that the penalty is far too large compared with the number of drivers affected. The company says that only 126 European drivers were deactivated because of low customer ratings in 2021. Uber also denies that permanent deactivations were ever fully automated. The size of the penalty also stands out historically because only Meta Platforms' (META) €1.2 billion GDPR fine from 2023 has been larger. Meta is appealing that decision as well.

Still, major European fines against U.S. technology companies can take years in court, and some have eventually been reduced or overturned. Therefore, investors should not automatically assume Uber will ultimately pay the full amount.

data.title: U.S. Military Says It Helped Move 660 Million Barrels of Oil Through Strait of Hormuz
data.description:
The U.S. military says it has helped tankers transport more than 660 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz waterway near Iran since May of this year. U.S. Central Command says the U.S. military assisted 1,300 commercial vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz in recent months. This suggests more than seven million barrels of oil per day has shipped through the Strait in the past three weeks.

The shipments claimed by the U.S. military are larger than private sector estimates but still less than half the 20 million barrels per day of crude oil that passed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the Iran war erupting earlier this year. Still, the U.S. military says that a substantial amount of crude oil is passing through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iran's ongoing attacks on ships in the waterway.

Conflicting Accounts

Exactly how much oil is coming out of Strait of Hormuz each day remains unclear. Both the U.S. and Iranian governments continue to provide conflicting and changing estimates that are usually much higher or lower than data from independent shipping companies and commodities tracking firms. The Trump administration recently claimed that 10 million barrels a day exited the Strait in recent weeks.

Maritime intelligence firm Windward estimates that crude oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz averaged about five million barrels a day in July, four million barrels per day in June, and only 1.6 million barrels a day in May of this year. The Trump administration recently abandoned military action in Iran and has moved instead to applying economic sanctions on the country.

Brent crude oil, the international standard, is trading at just under $94 a barrel on Aug. 21, having risen more than 5% in the past week.

That suggests NVDA is not as expensive as some peers based on expected earnings. The upcoming earnings report could test whether that lower valuation is justified.

For retail investors, full-year revenue guidance may matter more than the headline earnings beat.

What Experts Say About Nvidia's Valuation

Some experts see Nvidia as undervalued despite its strong AI growth and premium position in the chip market. EMJ Capital Founder and President Eric Jackson said Nvidia stock has been "cheap for a while." He noted that smaller AI chip players such as Marvell (MRVL) can trade at higher multiples because they are smaller and investors expect faster growth from them.

Morningstar also sees value in Nvidia. The firm said investors have shifted toward other AI semiconductor plays, including memory and optical chip stocks. Still, it sees upside for Nvidia if the company stays on track to meet its near- and medium-term revenue targets.

Meanwhile, Bank of America's analyst Vivek Arya is even more bullish on the valuation. His sum-of-the-parts analysis suggests Nvidia's free cash flow could be valued 34% to 50% higher than the current stock price, even after factoring in financing risks. He said investors may be overstating those risks, creating a "compelling opportunity."

Arya expects Nvidia to provide more details on its off-balance-sheet commitments when it reports earnings on August 26. Earlier this week, he reiterated his Buy rating and $350 price target on NVDA stock.

What Analysts Expect From Nvidia's Q2 Earnings

Heading into earnings, Wall Street remains highly bullish on NVDA, with 32 out of 33 analysts giving the stock a Buy rating. Analysts expect EPS of $2.09, nearly double the $1.05 reported a year ago. Revenue is forecast to jump 95% year-over-year to $92.04 billion.
